events.title: US-Iran Tensions Escalate
events.summary: The US and Iran are engaged in a heated standoff, with the US demanding reparations and Iran refusing to back down. This has led to a significant increase in oil prices, with US oil rising above $83 a barrel. The situation is highly volatile and could lead to further escalation.
events.reasoning: The escalation of tensions between the US and Iran has led to a significant increase in oil prices, making oil services stocks more attractive. On the other hand, the uncertainty and volatility in the market make it a good time to short government bonds.

timeFrame.note: Monitor the situation closely and be prepared to exit if tensions ease

events.exitStrategy: Exit if oil prices drop below $75 a barrel or if tensions ease significantly

events.summary: The Japanese yen has erased about half of the gains from an unprecedented US-Japan intervention less than two weeks ago. This has led to concerns about the effectiveness of the intervention.
events.reasoning: The failure of the US-Japan intervention to halt the yen slide makes it a good time to buy the yen, as it may continue to weaken.
